title: Grill round 2 — harness stacks fix round
summary: Three follow-ups on round 1: your **switch after the turn ends** choice needs two details, your note on the picker can be read two ways, and you asked **why the history has a cap**.
proven: Round 1 is recorded in `docs/plans/harness-stacks-fix-round-grill/round-1/answers.json` (19 recommendations accepted).

sections.title: Switch to next account — after the current turn
sections.intro: Round 1: *"Switch after the current turn ends"* (you turned down interrupting the live turn).

questions.title: On a task with no live run, does "Switch to next account" move right away?

options.label: Yes — move now
options.description: Same as today's same-stack switch: mirror, copy the conversation, "Switched to X — continuing this conversation".

options.label: No — move just before the next Run/message
options.description: The request is stored and applied lazily.

recommendation.reason: Nothing to wait for, and the header then shows the account the next message goes to.

questions.title: A switch is scheduled during a live turn. What happens when that turn ends?
questions.why: The turn can end in several ways; each needs a rule.
questions.context: In every option: the scheduled request is persisted (survives a core restart), the button turns into **Cancel scheduled switch**, and a provider limit during the turn is handled by the normal failover (which already moves the task), so the request is simply cleared.

options.label: Move only after a successful turn
options.description: Succeeded → move. Failed, Stop or cancelled → the request is dropped with a status line "scheduled switch cancelled".

options.label: Move whenever the turn ends
options.description: Succeeded, failed or stopped → move (a Stop still moves the task).

options.label: Move unless the user pressed Stop
options.description: Succeeded or failed → move; Stop drops the request.

recommendation.reason: A failed turn is often the reason to leave the account, while Stop means the user wants to take back control.

questions.title: Your note: "we should not have this type of picker for out of the stack." Which did you mean?
questions.context: Today the RunPanel's Harness picker lists **every** account. Picking an account outside the task's stack switches with a fresh session; picking one inside it keeps the conversation.

options.label: For a stacked task, list only the stack's accounts
options.description: Outside accounts disappear from the picker for a task on a stack. Leaving the stack is done with `agetor edit --agent` or by editing the stack.
options.consequence: The CLI keeps accepting any account.

options.label: Stack's accounts only — and refuse outside switches everywhere
options.description: PATCH /tasks/:id refuses (409) an account outside the task's stack, for the webview and the CLI.
options.consequence: A stacked task can only leave its stack by editing the stack.

options.label: Keep listing every account, but without the grouping/labels I proposed
options.description: Only add the cooling mark and the pending state.

recommendation.reason: Matches your note for the picker while keeping a deliberate escape hatch in the CLI.

questions.title: Keep the per-stack history without a cap?
questions.context: You asked why a cap. Honest numbers: a row is about 300 bytes, so 20 swaps a day for a year is ~7,300 rows, about 2 MB. Rows are deleted with the stack. The cap only guarded against unbounded growth; the real cost is rendering a long list, which pagination solves.

options.label: No cap; the view and the CLI page through it
options.description: Settings shows the latest 50 with "Load more"; `agetor harness stack history <stack> --limit N`.

recommendation.reason: The data is tiny and a cap would silently drop the history you might need when auditing a bad week.
